title: India's Youth-Led Movement Demands Education Minister's Resignation Over Examination Irregularities
text:
A youth-led movement in India has been gaining momentum over alleged examination irregularities and repeated paper leaks in the country's fiercely competitive college entrance exams. The protest, led by the Cockroach Janta Party, demands the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and seeks sweeping reforms to the examination system.

The protest, led by the Cockroach Janta Party, demands the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and seeks sweeping reforms to the examination system. The movement, which began in May, has amassed over 21 million Instagram followers and has drawn professionals beyond the world of education, including climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, who is undertaking an indefinite hunger strike. Despite the government's lack of response, the protest has continued, with thousands of supporters gathering at universities and rallies in other cities.
The movement has gained high-profile attention, with opposition leaders and Bollywood celebrities lending support. The protesters are also seeking compensation for families of students who died by suicide, whether over the leaks or exam results. The movement's leader, Abhijeet Dipke, has stated that the protesters will not resort to riots in the streets and that the hunger strike is a peaceful way to take their voice to the government.
The protest has been ongoing for weeks, with supporters enduring monsoon rain and sleeping in tents at the designated public protest ground, Jantar Mantar. The movement's demands include the resignation of the education minister, sweeping reforms to the examination system, and compensation for families of students who died by suicide. The protesters believe that the examination system is flawed and that the government is not taking adequate measures to address the issue.
They are calling for a more transparent and fair examination system, where students can compete on an equal footing. The movement has gained significant attention, with many young Indians seeing their future depending on a single entrance exam for government jobs and medical colleges. The protesters are determined to continue their peaceful protest until their demands are met. The government's response to the movement has been criticized, with many feeling that the government is not taking the issue seriously enough.
The movement's leader has stated that the protesters will not back down until their demands are met. The protest has become a symbol of the youth's frustration with the current education system and their desire for change. The movement's demands are not just limited to the education sector, but also reflect a broader desire for reform in the country's institutions and systems.
The protesters believe that a more just and equitable society can be achieved through peaceful means and that their movement is a step in the right direction. The protest has also drawn attention to the issue of student mental health, with many students feeling anxious and stressed about the exams.
